newsitem.title: GERMANY: F.O. LICHT - Daily coffee report.
newsitem.headline: F.O. LICHT - Daily coffee report.

text.p: The following is a direct contribution from statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

Robusta futures in London closed mixed after fluctuating in a modest range despite firmer New York values. November gave up $17 to close at $1,336 while January lost $2 to close at $1,328. News that Brazil supports a request by African coffee producing countries for a producer meeting to tighten the retention scheme came as somewhat of a surprise as initial indications were, that the Brazilians are not interested. Colombia, Ivory Coast and Uganda recently agreed on a need to increase the amount of coffee withheld under the ACPC retention scheme during the first half of 1997 by about 2.5 million 60-kg bags to shore up prices. Even though Brazil supports an emergency meeting official sources said the country has no position on the proposal to cut exports by 2.5 million bags.

In New York arabica futures ended higher in volatile dealings, as sharp gains in the spot December contract lifted the rest of the market. December added 6.00 cents/lb to close at 129.40 cents/lb, while March was 1.35 cents/lb higher to close at 111.20 cents/lb. In spite of the strong performance today it is still expected that new crop arrivals will increase and ease the prompt supply shortfall. It was added that many producers have been rushing to sell December, but the amount of coffee available was still limited. It was added with the likelihood of prices softening into the first quarter, more coffee will become available against the March contract.

The United States Department of Agriculture increased its forecast for 1996/97 world green coffee production to 100.9 million 60-kg bags, up 1.8 million bags from its estimate of 99.1 million in June and significantly higher than 1995/96 production of 89.9 million bags. The USDA estimate looks a little bearish but overall should have no significant impact on prices.

USDA - On Dec 13 the USDA forecast 1996/97 world green coffee production at 100.9 million 60-kg bags, up 1.8 million bags from its estimate of 99.1 million bags in June. Production last year was put at 89.9 million bags. The USDA revised its 1996/97 crop estimate for Brazil to 27 million bags, down from 27.5 million in June, which came as somewhat of a surprise. However, a greater surprise were the estimates for Mexico and Central America. Traders had expected to see lower forecasts for Mexico and some Central American countries, following heavy rainfall and flooding in the region in October. The USDA pegged Mexico's output at 5.4 million bags, from 4.7 million forecast in June, while Guatemala's coffee crop increased to 3.93 million bags from 3.5 million bags. Costa Rica's production was revised slightly, dipping to 2.5 million bags from 2.55 million bags.

Elsewhere, number-two grower Colombia's 1996/97 coffee output was pegged at 12.5 million bags, unchanged from a revised USDA estimate published last month. As expected, robusta coffee crops from Indonesia and Vietnam were raised. Indonesia's 1996/97 production is estimated at 7.5 million bags, from the 6.5 million bags seen in June. By comparison, Indonesia's drought-hit 1995/96 crop totalled 6.0 million bags. Vietnam's 1996/97 coffee production was forecast to come in at 4.3 million bags, up from 3.5 million bags seen previously, the USDA said. The USDA gave no estimate for consumption in 1996/97. However, there seems to be general consensus that offtake will be between 98 and 100 million bags in 1996/97 pointing to a more or less balanced situation based on the USDA production estimate.

DENMARK - Denmark imported 80,269 bags of coffee in September 1996, 4.6 percent less than was imported the same month the previous year. That brought total imports since the beginning of 1996 to 742,600 bags, 19 percent more than was imported the same period 1995. Total imports in calendar 1995 dropped by 14 percent to 873,700 bags. Major suppliers of green coffee in January/September 1996 were Brazil (178,800 vs 240,400 bags) and Colombia (153,400 vs 131,200 bags). The country exported 71,000 bags of coffee in January/September 1996, 9.2 percent more than in the same period in 1995. Total exports in calendar 1995 dropped by 5.5 percent to 91,200 bags.
